name: Sacroiliac Joint Pain / Dysfunction
definition: Pain arising from the sacroiliac joint complex or adjacent ligamentous structures. Diagnosis is clinical and probabilistic; clusters of provocation tests are more useful than a single maneuver.

typical: Pain near the posterior superior iliac spine or buttock
Pain with transfers, stairs, prolonged standing or turning in bed

redFlags.item: Major neurological deficit or malignancy concern

investigations.principle: Routine imaging does not confirm mechanical SI pain.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when inflammatory sacroiliitis, infection or stress fracture is suspected.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs may help characterize structural/inflammatory change in context.

green: Education, graded activity and hip/trunk rehabilitation
Address biomechanical and pregnancy/postpartum factors when relevant
amber: Image-guided diagnostic or therapeutic injection may be considered in selected persistent cases after adequate assessment.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Kati/Shroni-region pain may be documented as a phenotype correlation only.

patientEducation.summary: Pain arising from the sacroiliac joint complex or adjacent ligamentous structures. Diagnosis is clinical and probabilistic; clusters of provocation tests are more useful than a single maneuver.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal/joint pain, major trauma, or other listed red flags.
